html:
Margaret I ruled Denmark, Norway and Sweden at the end of the 1300s and joined them in the Kalmar Union, the largest state in northern Europe.

She was the daughter of the Danish king Valdemar IV and married King Haakon VI of Norway. After her father, husband and son died she ruled both kingdoms on behalf of others, and in 1389 her forces defeated the Swedish king. In 1397 her young great-nephew Eric of Pomerania was crowned king of all three at Kalmar.

The union lasted, with breaks, until Sweden left in 1523, but Denmark and Norway stayed together until 1814. Margaret is remembered as one of the ablest rulers of medieval Scandinavia. The union also tied the trade of the north to Copenhagen.
